name: orthonormal-range
title: Preserve basis vectors across finite column scales
head: 9cd05e45234e7e904c507b81c9309c0496ec1adb
body:
### Code of Conduct

I have read the project's Code of Conduct.

### Description

An unscaled norm can overflow or underflow even though every input component is finite. `vectorspace_orthonormalization` then replaces a nonzero basis vector with zeros. For example, multiplying the orthogonal columns `[[0.6, -0.8], [0.8, 0.6]]` by `1e200` returns a zero matrix; `1e-200` also loses both columns when `eps=0`.

Rescale columns whose magnitudes require it before projection and normalization, and carry the absolute residual threshold into the same scale. Ordinary columns retain their existing arithmetic. Add coverage for orthogonal and nonorthogonal inputs, finite vectors with an unrepresentable unscaled norm, mixed scales, exact dependent/zero columns, threshold boundaries, empty shapes, and input preservation.

### Related issues or pull requests

Fixes #1303. The issue was opened before implementing the patch. This changes the basis calculation; the separate dimensionality-rounding proposal #1227 is unchanged.

### Validation

[Exact-base reproduction and full-suite checks](https://github.com/Afloat16/geoopt/actions/runs/43863617417/job/133286456225):

- Production base `1aee767`: 12 failing regression cases and 8 passing controls.
- Patched math suite: **25 passed**, with **100% statement and branch coverage** of `math/linalg.py`.
- Full repository suite: **760 passed, 3 skipped**.
- Repository-wide isort and Black checks passed. Changed-file Flake8 and `git diff --check` passed; the repository-wide Flake8 report retains the existing W293 at `frequent_patterns/tests/test_association_rules.py:62`.

[Final-tree and package verification](https://github.com/Afloat16/geoopt/actions/runs/43864707589/job/133290176431) confirms the committed files exactly match those tested, and both the wheel and source distribution pass strict Twine checks. The first validation job's final artifact glob also included `dist/.gitignore`; this follow-up corrects that verification-script mistake without changing the tested production code.

Linux, Python 3.11.18, NumPy 2.4.0, SciPy 1.16.3, scikit-learn 1.8.0, pandas 2.3.3, using the unchanged frozen uv lock.

### Pull Request Checklist

- [x] Added a changelog entry.
- [x] Added regression and control tests.
- [x] Updated the API docstring to describe the absolute threshold.
- [x] Ran the full repository suite and focused branch-coverage checks.
- [x] Checked formatting and lint.
- User Guide notebook changes are not applicable to this numerical correction.

name: qr-rank-deficient
title: Fit QR linear regression on underdetermined and rank-deficient designs
head: b4baa76d7f4c95e2999770c224bcdbde49005269
body:
### Code of Conduct

I have read the project's Code of Conduct.

### Description

The QR solver explicitly inverts `R`. When the augmented design has more columns than observations, `R` is rectangular and fitting raises `LinAlgError`. A singular or numerically rank-deficient design can also produce undefined or arbitrary coefficients.

Use SciPy's rank-revealing, pivoted QR least-squares driver (`gelsy`) with a precision- and shape-dependent rank threshold. This preserves the existing fitted attribute shapes and returns a minimum-norm solution, including the intercept, when the coefficient vector is nonunique. The other solver paths are unchanged.

### Related issues or pull requests

Fixes #1304. The issue was opened before implementing the patch. The QR/SVD alternatives were introduced by #575; #1290 addresses Adaline's analytical path, which this PR does not modify.

### Validation

[Exact-base reproduction and full-suite checks](https://github.com/Afloat16/geoopt/actions/runs/43863617417/job/133286457424):

- Production base `1aee767`: 19 failing regression cases and 3 passing controls.
- Patched new and existing linear-regression tests: **38 passed**.
- Independent SVD pseudoinverse references cover wide, duplicate, constant, zero, rank-deficient and full-rank designs across float32, float64 and integer feature arrays. Tests also check residual orthogonality, read-only input preservation, fitted attribute shapes and refitting with a different feature count.
- Full repository suite: **762 passed, 3 skipped**.
- Repository-wide isort and Black checks passed. Changed-file Flake8 and `git diff --check` passed; the repository-wide Flake8 report retains the existing W293 at `frequent_patterns/tests/test_association_rules.py:62`.

[Final-tree and package verification](https://github.com/Afloat16/geoopt/actions/runs/43864707589/job/133290176736) confirms the committed files exactly match those tested, and both the wheel and source distribution pass strict Twine checks. The first validation job's final artifact glob also included `dist/.gitignore`; this follow-up corrects that verification-script mistake without changing the tested production code.

Linux, Python 3.11.18, NumPy 2.4.0, SciPy 1.16.3, scikit-learn 1.8.0, pandas 2.3.3, using the unchanged frozen uv lock.

### Pull Request Checklist

- [x] Added a changelog entry.
- [x] Added regression and control tests.
- [x] Documented the QR solver's rank-deficient behavior.
- [x] Ran the full repository suite and focused coverage checks.
- [x] Checked formatting and lint.
- User Guide notebook changes are not applicable to this solver correction.

name: apriori-sparse-low-memory
title: Keep low-memory Apriori support counting sparse
head: 00039441e569753ed772a18fe5973bf606406ad6
body:
### Code of Conduct

I have read the project's Code of Conduct.

### Description

Sparse input currently becomes dense inside `generate_new_combinations_low_memory`: both the prefix columns and all candidate columns are converted with `toarray()`. This can allocate a large dense block even when very few transactions contain the prefix.

Keep prefix matching and candidate support counts sparse. Reduce prefix rows, select only matching transactions, and then reduce candidate columns. Canonicalize the sliced sparse matrices so duplicate Boolean entries retain the logical values produced by the previous dense conversion; explicit stored zeros do not count as present items. Candidate generation, support thresholds, result ordering, and the caller's sparse storage are preserved.

In a repeatable 50,000-by-500 input with 500 nonzeros, the median peak allocation for candidate enumeration falls from **25,071,606 to 861,899 bytes** across three measurements (about **96.6% less**). This is a measured allocation result for that workload, not a general runtime claim.

### Related issues or pull requests

Fixes #1308, opened before implementation. #619 introduced the sparse low-memory path; this patch removes its remaining dense support-counting intermediates. The earlier sparse-format, Boolean-input, and candidate-generation changes were checked for overlap.

### Validation

[Exact-base reproduction, benchmark, full suite, and package checks](https://github.com/Afloat16/geoopt/actions/runs/43867750166/job/133300579334):

- Base `1aee767`: **20 failing regressions and 1 passing dense control**.
- Patched frequent-pattern suites: **132 passed**.
- Full repository suite: **761 passed, 3 skipped**.
- Regressions cover CSC/CSR matrices and arrays, Boolean and uint8 data, brute-force support oracles, pandas sparse input, explicit zeros, duplicate Boolean storage, a 257-item prefix, empty matching rows, and unchanged inputs.
- Repository-wide isort and Black checks, changed-file Flake8, `git diff --check`, wheel/source builds, and strict Twine checks pass. Repository-wide Flake8 retains the pre-existing W293 at `frequent_patterns/tests/test_association_rules.py:62`.

Validation uses Python 3.11.18 and the unchanged frozen uv lock (NumPy 2.4.0, SciPy 1.16.3, scikit-learn 1.8.0, pandas 2.3.3). A [separate exact-base check](https://github.com/Afloat16/geoopt/actions/runs/43867750166/job/133300579092) reproduces the current upstream linter's Python 3.15.2 dependency-installation failure: locked SciPy 1.16.3 attempts a source build and cannot find OpenBLAS, before any style check runs.

### Pull Request Checklist

- [x] Added a changelog entry.
- [x] Added regression and control tests.
- [x] Updated the low-memory API documentation.
- [x] Ran the full repository suite.
- [x] Checked formatting and lint.
- User Guide notebook changes are not applicable to this internal memory correction.

name: minmax-finite-range
title: Preserve finite results when min-max scaling ranges overflow
head: a08bba3825b275cc1e0d84e95f57087c88626b5d
body:
### Code of Conduct

I have read the project's Code of Conduct.

### Description

`minmax_scaling` can return NaN or infinity although its inputs and requested output bounds are finite. For example, scaling `[-1e308, 0, 1e308]` to [0, 1] overflows while subtracting the extrema. An output interval spanning the floating-point limits can similarly overflow when its width is formed.

Halve input columns only when their magnitudes require it before forming differences, preserving the same normalized ratios. For output intervals whose width cannot be represented, interpolate between the finite endpoints without constructing that width. Ordinary columns retain the existing arithmetic, and constant columns retain their current mapping.

### Related issues or pull requests

Fixes #1309, opened before implementation. This addresses overflow in finite input and output ranges. The earlier single-endpoint condition change (#1210), constant-column handling, and DataFrame-selection proposals address different cases; their behavior is retained here.

### Validation

[Exact-base reproduction, full suite, and package checks](https://github.com/Afloat16/geoopt/actions/runs/43867750166/job/133300579285):

- Base `1aee767`: **27 failing regressions and 11 passing controls**.
- Patched preprocessing suites: **82 passed**.
- Full repository suite: **778 passed, 3 skipped**.
- Expected values come from an independent 400-digit Decimal calculation. Cases cover both floating-point extremes, ordinary and constant columns, reversed output ranges, one-dimensional input, selected DataFrame columns, column/index preservation, and unchanged caller input.
- Repository-wide isort and Black checks, changed-file Flake8, `git diff --check`, wheel/source builds, and strict Twine checks pass. Repository-wide Flake8 retains the pre-existing W293 at `frequent_patterns/tests/test_association_rules.py:62`.

Validation uses Python 3.11.18 and the unchanged frozen uv lock (NumPy 2.4.0, SciPy 1.16.3, scikit-learn 1.8.0, pandas 2.3.3). A [separate exact-base check](https://github.com/Afloat16/geoopt/actions/runs/43867750166/job/133300579092) reproduces the current upstream linter's Python 3.15.2 dependency-installation failure: locked SciPy 1.16.3 attempts a source build and cannot find OpenBLAS, before any style check runs.

### Pull Request Checklist

- [x] Added a changelog entry.
- [x] Added regression and control tests.
- [x] Updated the API docstring for finite-range handling.
- [x] Ran the full repository suite.
- [x] Checked formatting and lint.
- User Guide notebook changes are not applicable to this numerical correction.
